finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl allows arbitrary file read. filepath.Join(root, name) cleans the path but does not confine it to root, so f=../../../../etc/passwd resolves to /etc/passwd and is returned.
finding.source: Query parameter 'f' (files.go:12) via r.URL.Query().Get("f"); server listens on all interfaces on :8082 (files.go:34).
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13; contents written to response at files.go:18.

trace.note: name := r.URL.Query().Get("f") takes raw attacker-controlled value
filepath.Join(root, name) with root=/srv/files (files.go:9) calls Clean, resolving .. segments above root; no containment check
w.Write(data) returns file contents to the caller

finding.guards_checked: filepath.Join performs no containment; no prefix check, filepath.Rel, filepath.IsLocal, filepath.Base, allowlist, or authentication on /dl. Error path (files.go:14-16) returns generic 404 and does not prevent exploitation. Impact: any file readable by the server process (config, .env, keys, source). Confidence high from code reading; Go Clean semantics not executed.

verdict.guard_found: none. /dl (files.go:11-19) has no authentication, no path containment (no filepath.Rel, IsLocal, prefix check, or Base), and no allowlist. The only error handling (files.go:14-16) returns a 404 and does not block the read. The filepath.Base at files.go:22 applies only to the /avatar handler, not /dl.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: files.go:12 takes the raw "f" query value, files.go:13 joins it onto root with filepath.Join, which Clean-resolves ".." segments above /srv/files (so "../../../../etc/passwd" becomes /etc/passwd), and files.go:18 writes the file contents back to an anonymous caller. The server listens on all interfaces on :8082 (files.go:34), so an unauthenticated remote attacker can read any file the process can access.

finding.claim: No authentication or authorization on any endpoint. /dl and /avatar are registered without middleware, so anyone who can reach port 8082 can download every file under /srv/files, even if F1 is fixed. Whether this is a defect depends on whether /dl is meant to serve only public files.
finding.source: Any network client reaching port 8082 (files.go:34 listens on all interfaces).
finding.sink: Reading files under /srv/files via download handler (files.go:32, files.go:11-19).

trace.note: http.HandleFunc("/dl", download) registers handler with no auth middleware
http.ListenAndServe(":8082", nil) exposes it on all interfaces
download handler performs no identity or permission check before reading

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, token or session check, IP restriction, or middleware present on either route. Separate authorization failure from F1. Policy-dependent: reported as high with intent caveat.

verdict.guard_found: none. files.go:32-34 register /dl and /avatar directly on the default mux with no middleware, and ListenAndServe(":8082") binds all interfaces. The download handler (files.go:11-19) reads filepath.Join(root, name) with no identity, session, token, or IP check. The only check is the os.ReadFile error path (files.go:14-16), which is not an access control.
verdict.reason: Any anonymous client that can reach port 8082 reaches the unauthenticated download handler at files.go:32 and reads any file under /srv/files via files.go:13 with no guard between them. Whether this is a defect depends on whether everything under /srv/files is meant to be public, and nothing in the code states that intent, so the report should keep the policy caveat.
